central_question: Across the exact scheduled four-hour Cross lifecycles, does the unhedged common US30/US500 component contribute large, near-zero-mean variance that materially dilutes the signed relative component, and if so at what frozen lot-staircase capital can a three-leg 0.5/0.5 notional hedge first be represented within ten-percent weight tolerance?

common_beta.direction_failure: Both directions passed common variance, removable variance and positive relative mean, but relative quality was lower than total quality in each direction.

capital_granularity.reference_100_usd: At 0.01 US100 lot, US30 is forced to 0.01 and realizes 1.67 to 3.08 of US100 notional instead of 0.5; zero of 756 states satisfy the US30 weight tolerance. US500 uses 0.01 or 0.02 and satisfies its tolerance in 26.59 percent of states.
capital_granularity.portfolio_boundary: A three-leg expression reserves 12 percent planned risk and all three slots, leaving zero capacity for the other five components.

reason: The common path is quantitatively large, but it is not a near-zero-mean nuisance component whose removal improves Cross quality. Its pooled signed mean exceeds the frozen near-zero bound, only one of four periods passes that bound, and relative-only quality is about half of total quality. All four periods and both directions fail the required quality improvement. The common component therefore carries part of the favorable signed return as well as variance; hedging it away is not supported by this bundle.

preserve: the existing directional single-leg US100 Cross construction
the descriptive lot-granularity observation that a 0.5/0.5 peer hedge becomes representable at median 550 USD and p90 1000 USD under current min/step sizes
discard: the claim that near-zero-mean common beta materially dilutes Cross
a capital-scaled three-leg Cross Lab candidate from Unit 064
any current portfolio insertion that would consume 12 percent risk and all three slots

no_rescue: alternate peer weights, OLS or rolling beta, PCA or volatility scaling
one-peer hedge, direction, period, volatility, feature-strength or outcome subgroup
stop-path tick reconstruction, cost rescue, tolerance relaxation or lot-search extension
immediate hedge EA, portfolio insertion, promotion or Live action
